This study investigates sodium reduction intervention for blood pressure control, not dietary fat intake. The primary outcomes are blood pressure effects and medication use, not measures of weight or body fatness. Does not meet criterion 3 (lower fat diet intervention) and criterion 5 (weight/body fatness outcome).

While this is an RCT with a lower fat diet intervention (20% of calories) in adult women without weight loss intention, the outcomes assessed are mental health variables (anxiety, depression, vigor) measured by the Mental Health Inventory. The study does not report any measures of weight or body fatness as outcomes. Fails criterion 5.

This is a follow-up survey examining maintenance of low-fat diet adherence after the Women\'s Health Trial ended. While it involves a lower fat diet intervention in adult women, the outcome measured is percentage of energy from fat (dietary adherence), not weight or body fatness. No weight/BMI/waist circumference data reported. Fails criterion 5.

This study examines the effect of low-fat diet on blood lipid levels (plasma cholesterol, phospholipins) in normal subjects and multiple sclerosis patients. The outcomes are exclusively lipid-related measures, with no assessment of weight or body fatness. Duration ranges from 5-13 months which meets the time criterion, but fails criterion 5 (no weight/body fatness outcome).

This thesis describes three controlled feeding trials comparing different fatty acid compositions. However, each diet was supplied for only 3 weeks per volunteer, which fails criterion 5 requiring at least 6 months duration. Additionally, outcomes are serum lipoproteins (LDL, HDL cholesterol), blood pressure, and Lp(a) - not weight or body fatness measures.

This is a systematic review of prospective cohort studies, not a primary RCT or cohort study. The selection criteria specify inclusion of primary trials and cohort studies, not systematic reviews/meta-analyses. Wrong study design.

This is a meta-analysis (Nordmann et al., Am J Med 2011) comparing Mediterranean to low-fat diets. As a meta-analysis rather than a primary RCT or cohort study, it does not meet the study design criteria. The focus is also on cardiovascular risk factors, not specifically weight/body fatness outcomes.

This is a Cochrane systematic review assessing effects of dietary fat reduction/modification on mortality and cardiovascular outcomes. It is not a primary RCT or cohort study. The objectives focus on cardiovascular morbidity/mortality and cancer diagnoses, not weight or body fatness outcomes.

This is a Cochrane systematic review on reducing saturated fat intake and its replacement with other macronutrients. It is not a primary RCT or cohort study. The outcomes assessed are mortality and cardiovascular morbidity, not weight or body fatness measures.
